<reason>A narrowly won by more convincingly distinguishing new exploitation from completing an already compensated role. B defended a meaningful protective default and coherently extended its principle to conventional fabrication. However, its descriptions of A’s alternative as unpaid or effectively unrestricted overstated the position. A answered the pressure questions directly and better explained why material alteration does not necessarily exceed production authority. B established genuine risks, but insufficiently justified requiring an explicit AI grant for otherwise authorized changes.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s response to the endorsement analogy was especially effective: attributing a personal commercial recommendation differs from shaping fictional dialogue within a commissioned role. Its later distinction between silence about a technique and unlimited permission reinforced that rebuttal and undercut B’s ownership framing.</best_rebuttal>
